summary: Prods Oktor Skjærvø works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the University of Oslo (PhD 1981) and Mainz (habil. 1984), and served as Aga Khan Professor of Iranian Studies at Harvard (~1993–2015).

Pulinbihari Chakravarti is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Curator of Manuscripts at The Asiatic Society (attested 1951).

Purnima Dhavan is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Virginia. She held posts at Bowdoin College, St. John's University, and the University of Washington, where she became Associate Professor in 2005.

Purushottam Mahadev Joshi was a historian and archaeologist. He worked at the University of Mumbai Library (~1935–1947) and later served as Reader in Medieval History at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1964–1974).

Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from the University of Mumbai (MA 1919) and Harvard (PhD 1932). He held posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University (1945–1948), and the University of Delhi (1957–1960).

Purushottama Bilimoria specializes in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Shivesh Thakur and completed his PhD at La Trobe University. His academic positions include Deakin University (attested 2001–2009) and the University of Melbourne (attested 2001–2016).
Puthezathu Rama Menon was an Indologist and legal official. He served as a judge on the Chief Court of Cochin and was president of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at King's College London by 2014 and later served there as a postdoctoral research fellow (attested 2017).

Péter-Dániel Szántó specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Balliol College, Oxford, under Alexis Sanderson, and has held positions at All Souls College, Oxford, and Eötvös Loránd University.
Qian Cao works in Indology and religious studies, serving as both a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Qian Lin works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied at Fudan University, the University of Bristol, and the University of Washington (PhD under Collett Cox), and later joined the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 2026).

Qiang Ning is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who completed his doctoral studies under Hung Wu and Irene Winter. He held teaching posts at Michigan, Yale, and San Diego State, and researched at Dunhuang Academy.

Qichao Liang worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying under Youwei Kang, he held posts at Shiwu Xuetang, the Translation Bureau, Nankai University, Tsinghua University, and the National Library of China (1925–1927).

Qing Duan was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University and the University of Hamburg (PhD under Ronald Eric Emmerick), and served as a professor at Peking University (~1987–2022).

Qingying Chen was a scholar of Tibetology and history. After studying under Wang Yao at Minzu University of China, he taught there and later served as director of the Historical Research Institute at the China Tibetology Research Center (~1993–2012).
Qingzhi Zhu is a scholar in linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who has held professorial posts at Peking University (attested 2004) and the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
Qinni Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
Qiwen Xiao is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under supervisor Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).
Qun Dai is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied at Bard College under the supervision of Patricia Eichenbaum Karetzky (attested 2016).
R. Balasubramanian was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under the traditional teacher Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. He served as Director at the University of Madras (~1975–1989).
